ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.claim: The fate of a wealthy Jewish capitalist shows that God grants favors, though the wretched attribute them to their own ability and idols.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.anchor: The fate of a capitalist Jew is mentioned.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r11.claim: After warning against arrogant joy, the people tell Qārūn to use God's wealth for afterlife reward through good works.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p324/r11.anchor: أمروه بأن يطلب، فيما آتاه الله من الكنوز وسعة الرزق، ثواب الدار الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most commentators say not to neglect one's share of worldly life means not wasting one's lifetime without good deeds, since the afterlife is earned here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، والجمهور: معناه: ولا تضيع عمرك في أن لا تعمل صالحا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda instead understand the phrase as permitting lawful enjoyment, seeking it, and prudent attention to worldly needs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن، وقتادة: معناه: لا تضيع حظك من الدنيا في تمتعك بالحلال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan also says to give away the surplus while retaining enough to live on.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه: قدم الفضل وأمسك ما تبلغ به.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r4.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r4.claim: Mālik glosses one's share as eating and drinking without extravagance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r4.anchor: وقال مالك: هو الأكل والشرب بلا سرف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r5.claim: Another admonition says that one's only worldly share of amassed wealth may be a shroud and burial spices, illustrated by a poem.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r5.anchor: وقيل: أرادوا بنصيبه الكفن، وهذا وعظ متصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says to take from worldly life what suffices and benefits you, close to al-Ḥasan's interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أن تأخذ منه ما يكفيك ويصلحك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r7.claim: “Do good as God did good to you” can use the kāf for comparison in a limited respect, or for causation: do good because God favored you.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r7.anchor: والكاف للتشبيه، وهو يكون في بعض الأوصاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r8.claim: “Do not seek corruption” rebukes Qārūn for the oppression he was already committing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p325/r8.anchor: ولا تبغ الفساد: أي ما أنت عليه من البغي والظلم.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r3.claim: Razi takes Qarun to acknowledge the afterlife: use God's gift of wealth for what leads to Paradise, while adopting humility.

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r4.claim: One possible reading is that Qarun was so absorbed in earning wealth that he neglected enjoyment, so the adviser told him to make time for it.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r4.anchor: لعله كان مستغرق الهم في طلب الدنيا فلأجل ذلك ما كان يتفرغ للتنعم والالتذاذ فنهاه الواعظ عن ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r5.claim: Another reading permits enjoyment of lawful worldly pleasures alongside the call to spend wealth for the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r5.anchor: لما أمره الواعظ بصرف المال إلى الآخرة بين له بهذا الكلام أنه لا بأس بالتمتع بالوجوه المباحة

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r6.claim: A third reading makes spending in God's obedience one's true share of worldly life, unlike merely eating and drinking.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r6.anchor: المراد منه الإنفاق في طاعة الله فإن ذلك هو نصيب المرء من الدنيا دون الذي يأكل ويشرب

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r7.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r7.claim: Razi quotes a prophetic exhortation to take from oneself for oneself, prepare in worldly life for the afterlife, and use youth and life before old age and death; after death only Paradise or Hell remains.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r7.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ( فليأخذ العبد من نفسه لنفسه

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r8.claim: The command extends beyond financial giving to all kindness, including help through wealth or status, a cheerful face, a warm welcome, and favorable mention.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r8.anchor: بالإحسان بالمال أمره بالإحسان مطلقا ويدخل فيه الإعانة بالمال

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r9.claim: Razi says the reminder to reciprocate God's beneficence evokes the promise that gratitude brings increase.

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r10.claim: The corruption forbidden here is the oppression and transgression Qarun practiced.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r10.anchor: والمراد ما كان عليه من الظلم والبغي

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r11.claim: Some identify Moses as the speaker of this admonition.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r11.anchor: وقيل إن هذا القائل هو موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r12.claim: Other interpreters identify the speaker as the believers among Qarun's own people.

RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r13.claim: Razi says this admonition was already complete and could not be improved, yet Qarun refused it and answered with ingratitude by claiming his wealth came from his own knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v25p14/r13.anchor: ما لو قيل لم يكن عليه مزيد

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r1.claim: The use of fīmā rather than bimā means seek the hereafter while in a state of ownership and capacity, with both wealth and bodily ability.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r1.anchor: لم يقل بما آتاك الله لأنه لم يرد بمالك وإنما أراد وابتغ في حال تملكك وفي حال قدرتك

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r2.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r2.claim: Kashf al-Asrar identifies the hereafter's reward as the goal, reached by using wealth for the poor, kin, captives, and other good causes.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r2.anchor: أي ثواب الله فيها بصرفه إلى ما يكون وسيلة إليه من مواساة الفقراء وصلة الرحم وفك الأسير

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r3.claim: A Persian couplet urges using worldly means to purchase the hereafter.

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r4.claim: Do not neglect your share as though it were forgotten; nisyān is losing what was entrusted through weak memory, distraction, or deliberate neglect.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r4.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : النسيان ترك الإنسان ضبط ما استودع

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r5.claim: One's worldly share is either what secures the hereafter or enough for one's needs, with the remainder given away.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r5.anchor: وهو أن تحصل بها آخرتك أو تأخذ منها ما يكفيك وتخرج الباقي

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r6.speaker: علي
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r6.claim: Ali explains the worldly share as one's health, strength, youth, and wealth.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r6.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه : لا تنس صحتك وقوتك وشبابك وغناك

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r7.claim: The Prophet advised a man to seize five opportunities before their opposites: youth before age, health before illness, wealth before poverty, free time before busyness, and life before death.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r7.anchor: وفي ذلك ما روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لرجل وهو يعظه :

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r8.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r8.claim: Kashifi says one's share on leaving this world will be a shroud, so one should consider departure and not be deluded by wealth.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r8.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (وفراموش مكن بهره خودرا ازمال دنيا

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r9.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r9.claim: Saadi's verse says that even a hero or swordsman cannot carry beyond a shroud when departing this world.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r9.anchor:
قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره :
اكرا هلواني اكر تيغ زن نخواهي بدر بردن الأكفن

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r10.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r10.claim: For a gnostic, the share of this world is the Prophet's three beloved things: fragrance, women, and the delight of prayer; these signify good scent, beauty, and joy of heart.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r10.anchor: وقال بعض العارفين : نصيب العارف من الدنيا ما أشار إليه عليه السلام بقوله

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r11.claim: The command is to treat God's servants well in return for God's beneficence to the addressee.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r11.anchor: {وأحسن} إلى عباد الله {كما أحسن الله إليك} فيما أنعم به عليك

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r12.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r12.claim: Saadi's verse urges the prosperous person to eat and give generously, thereby winning both this world and the next.
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r12.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره : توانكري ودل دوست كامرانت هست بخور ببخش

BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313#2/r13.claim: The author's couplet begins by imagining someone acquiring Qarun's treasure.

BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r1.claim: This prohibition addresses Qarun's own oppression and transgression.
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r1.anchor: نهى له عما كان عليك من الظلم والبغي

BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r2.claim: In the land of the spirit, corruption means using human spiritual potential to violate religious law and follow nature, thereby damaging human and spiritual preparedness.
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r2.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {ولا تبغ الفساد فى الأرض}

BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r3.claim: God loves reformers for good deeds; the chosen abdal replace ignorance with knowledge, miserliness with generosity, greed with chastity, injustice with justice, rashness with deliberation, and corruption with righteousness, rising to the beloved's rank.
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r3.anchor: فإنهم يجعلون بدل الجهل العلم وبدل الشح الجود وبدل الشره العفة وبدل الظلم العدالة

BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p313#3/r4.claim: The author's couplet continues that Qarun's treasure will not remain unless one gives it away.

STUDYQURAN:28:77/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r1.claim: Korah is told to use wealth for good works rather than waste it or hoard it; this advice applies generally.
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r1.anchor: use his wealth for good works, rather than wasting it or being miserly with it (Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:77/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r2.claim: One reading says not to waste life by neglecting good works, charity, or preparation for the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r2.anchor: by neglecting to do good works, be charitable, or prepare for the Hereafter (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:77/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r3.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r3.claim: Others understand the phrase as warning against extreme asceticism and detachment, and as permission to enjoy what God has made lawful.
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r3.anchor: others interpret it to mean that one should not go to extremes of asceticism and detachment from the world and enjoy what God has made permissible

STUDYQURAN:28:77/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r4.speaker: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī quotes Ibn ʿUmar: work for this world as if living forever and for the Hereafter as if dying tomorrow; the saying is sometimes attributed to the Prophet or ʿAlī.
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r4.anchor: Here al-Qurṭubī quotes a saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar (sometimes attributed to the Prophet or to ʿAlī)

STUDYQURAN:28:77/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r5.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r5.claim: Some say one’s portion in this world means one’s coffin or grave, evoking remembrance of death.
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r5.anchor: Some say that the portion in this world refers to one’s coffin or grave (Q)

STUDYQURAN:28:77/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r6.claim: The root ḥ-s-n in be good also carries the senses of beauty and virtue.
STUDYQURAN:28:77/r6.anchor: The root of good in And be good, as God has been good to you is ḥ-s-n, which also has the sense of beauty and virtue.

TAB-FULL:v18p321#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p321#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p321#2/r1.claim: Qarun should use the wealth God gave him to seek the good of the Hereafter by obeying God in this worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v18p321#2/r1.anchor: والتمس فيما آتاك الله من الأموال خيرات الآخرة بالعمل فيها بطاعة الله في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v18p321#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p321#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p321#2/r2.claim: His people warn Qarun not to oppress them on account of his great wealth.
TAB-FULL:v18p321#2/r2.anchor: لا تبغ يا قارون على قومك بكثرة مالك

TAB-FULL:v18p323/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says not to leave doing work for God in this life, but to work in it for the Hereafter.
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا، وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك} [القصص: 77] يقول: لا تترك أن تعمل لله في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v18p323/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r2.speaker: عون بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r2.claim: Awn says people misplace the meaning: the share to remember is work in obedience to God.
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r2.anchor: عن عون بن عبد الله، " {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} [القصص: 77] قال: إن قوما يضعونها على غير موضعها

TAB-FULL:v18p323/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r3.claim: Mujahid repeatedly interprets the share as obedience to God and working in worldly life for the Hereafter.
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} [القصص: 77] قال: العمل بطاعته

TAB-FULL:v18p323/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says to send good deeds ahead from worldly provision, since one finds in the Hereafter what one sent ahead in this life.
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} [القصص: 77] قال: لا تنس أن تقدم من دنياك لآخرتك

TAB-FULL:v18p323/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r5.claim: Another group instead understands the instruction as not neglecting to seek one’s share of worldly provision.
TAB-FULL:v18p323/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: لا تترك أن تطلب فيها حظك من الرزق

TAB-FULL:v18p324/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the worldly share is what God made lawful, which gives a person sufficiency.
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: " {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} [القصص: 77] : قال الحسن: «ما أحل الله لك منها، فإن لك فيه غنى وكفاية»

TAB-FULL:v18p324/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r2.claim: Qatadah glosses the worldly share as seeking lawful provision.
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: " {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} [القصص: 77] قال: طلب الحلال

TAB-FULL:v18p324/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r3.claim: Al-Hasan advises giving the surplus and keeping what suffices for one’s needs.
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r3.anchor: عن الحسن: " {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} [القصص: 77] : قال: قدم الفضل، وأمسك ما يبلغك

TAB-FULL:v18p324/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the phrase means lawful provision in this worldly life.

TAB-FULL:v18p324/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r5.claim: Do good by spending the wealth God gave you in its proper ways, just as God expanded and made provision abundant for you.
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r5.anchor: وأحسن في الدنيا إنفاق مالك الذي آتاكه الله، في وجوهه وسبله، كما أحسن الله إليك، فوسع عليك منه

TAB-FULL:v18p324/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the command as doing good with what God has provided.
TAB-FULL:v18p324/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك} [القصص: 77] قال: أحسن فيما رزقك الله

TABATABAI:28:76-78/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r2.claim: Use the worldly wealth God gave you to build the hereafter by spending it in God’s cause and in ways that please Him.
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r2.anchor: أي واطلب فيما أعطاك الله من مال الدنيا تعمير الدار الآخرة بإنفاقه في سبيل الله ووضعه فيما فيه مرضاته تعالى

TABATABAI:28:76-78/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r3.claim: Do not neglect the share God allotted and provided; put it to work for the afterlife, since a person’s true share is what they do for the next life and what remains for them.
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r3.anchor: أي لا تترك ما قسم الله لك ورزقك من الدنيا ترك المنسي واعمل فيه لآخرتك لأن حقيقة نصيب الإنسان من الدنيا هو ما يعمل به لآخرته

TABATABAI:28:76-78/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r4.claim: A view says one’s worldly share is small: enough food, drink, and clothing for oneself, leaving excess to others; Tabataba’i calls this good and says other views do not suit the context.
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r4.anchor: وقيل معناه لا تنس أن نصيبك من الدنيا - وقد أقبلت عليك - شيء قليل مما أوتيت وهو ما تأكله وتشربه

TABATABAI:28:76-78/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r5.claim: Spend on others in kindness as God kindly gave to you without your deserving it; this restates the first reading of worldly share or completes the second.
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r5.anchor: أي أنفقه لغيرك إحسانا كما آتاكه الله إحسانا من غير ان تستحقه وتستوجبه

TABATABAI:28:76-78/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r6.claim: Do not use wealth, status, or influence to seek corruption; God does not love corrupters because creation is grounded in goodness and reform.
TABATABAI:28:76-78/r6.anchor: أي لا تطلب الفساد في الأرض بالاستعانة بما آتاك الله من مال وما اكتسبت به من جاه وحشمة

TABRISI:28:77-78/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:77-78/r1.claim: The advice is usually attributed to Qarun’s believing kinsmen; another view says Moses addressed him in the plural.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r1.anchor: وهذا أيضا من مقالة المؤمنين من قوم قارون له. وقيل: إن المخاطب له بذلك موسى

TABRISI:28:77-78/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:77-78/r2.claim: Use God’s wealth to seek the afterlife by spending it on good works and charity.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r2.anchor: اطلب فيما أعطاك الله من الأموال الدار الآخرة بأن تنفقها في سبيل الخير

TABRISI:28:77-78/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:77-78/r3.claim: Most exegetes take this to mean doing worldly deeds for the afterlife: one’s true share of this life is what benefits the next.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r3.anchor: وهو أن تعمل في الدنيا للآخرة عن أكثر المفسرين ومعناه لا تنس أن تعمل لآخرتك

TABRISI:28:77-78/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r4.speaker: علي
TABRISI:28:77-78/r4.claim: ʿAlī explains one’s worldly share as health, strength, free time, youth, energy, and wealth, which one should use to seek the afterlife.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r4.anchor: وروي في معناه عن علي ع لا تنس صحتك وقوتك وفراغك وشبابك

TABRISI:28:77-78/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r5.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:28:77-78/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Qarun was told to give away the surplus while retaining enough to suffice him.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r5.anchor: أمر أن يقدم الفضل وأن يمسك ما يغنيه عن الحسن

TABRISI:28:77-78/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:77-78/r6.claim: Another explanation says the miserly Qarun was told he could eat, drink, and lawfully enjoy what God gave him.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r6.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه كان فتورا شحيحا فقيل له كل واشرب واستمتع

TABRISI:28:77-78/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:77-78/r7.claim: Give generously to people as God has been generous to Qarun.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r7.anchor: أي أفضل على الناس كما أفضل الله عليك

TABRISI:28:77-78/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r8.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
TABRISI:28:77-78/r8.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Sallām says it means to fulfill God’s obligations as God has bestowed blessings.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r8.anchor: أحسن فيما افترض الله عليك كما أحسن في إنعامه عليك عن يحيى بن سلام

TABRISI:28:77-78/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:77-78/r9.claim: Another explanation combines thanking God according to His blessings with supporting God’s servants through one’s wealth.
TABRISI:28:77-78/r9.anchor: معناه وأحسن شكر الله تعالى على قدر إنعامه عليك وواس عباد الله بمالك

TABRISI:28:77-78/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:77-78/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:77-78/r10.claim: Do not seek to commit disobedience on earth.

THALABI:v7p261/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r9.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد؛ ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p261/r9.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd, also transmitted from Ibn Abbas through Ali ibn Abi Talha, say not to neglect working in this life for the afterlife and escape from punishment.
THALABI:v7p261/r9.anchor: قال مجاهد وابن زيد: لا تترك أن تعمل في دنياك لآخرتك حتى تنجو من عذاب الله، وهي رواية علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس

THALABI:v7p261/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r10.speaker: علي
THALABI:v7p261/r10.claim: Ali says to use one's health, strength, youth, energy, and wealth to seek the afterlife.
THALABI:v7p261/r10.anchor: وقال علي «رضي الله عنه» : لا تنس صحتك وقوتك وشبابك ونشاطك وغناك

THALABI:v7p261/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r11.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v7p261/r11.claim: Hasan says to seek from this world one's sufficiency and wealth through what God has made lawful.
THALABI:v7p261/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن: ولا تنس أن تطلب فيها كفايتك وغناك مما أحل الله لك منها

THALABI:v7p261/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r12.speaker: منصور بن زاذان
THALABI:v7p261/r12.claim: Mansur ibn Zadhan identifies one's share of this world as one's own sustenance and that of one's family.
THALABI:v7p261/r12.anchor: عن منصور بن زادان في قوله: ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا قال: قوتك وقوة أهلك

THALABI:v7p261/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p261/r13.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p261/r13.claim: Another view takes one's share to mean the shroud, one's worldly portion at departure from life.
THALABI:v7p261/r13.anchor: وقيل: هو الكفن لأنه حظه من الدنيا عند خروجه منها

THALABI:v7p262/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p262/r1.claim: The command is to treat people well as God has treated you well, and not to seek corruption on earth.
THALABI:v7p262/r1.anchor: وأحسن إلى الناس كما أحسن الله إليك ولا تبغ ولا تطلب الفساد في الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil explain seeking the afterlife as seeking Paradise through the wealth, blessings, abundance, and good things God gave.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r3.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains seeking Paradise through blessings as thanking God and spending one’s gifts in what pleases Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r3.anchor: والمعنى: اطلب فيما أنعم الله به عليك الجنة، وهو: أن يشكر الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r4.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās says one’s worldly share is doing what God loves and approves for His sake.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: يريد: العمل لله فيها بما يحب ويرضى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r5.claim: In al-Aʿmash’s transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās says to work in this world for the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r5.anchor: وقال في رواية الأعمش: أي: تعمل فيها لآخرتك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r6.claim: Muqātil, Mujāhid, and Ibn Zayd say not to neglect work for the afterlife, since a person’s true worldly share is what they do for it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r6.anchor: وهو قول مقاتل ومجاهد وابن زيد؛ قالوا: لا تترك أن تعمل لآخرتك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r7.speaker: الوالبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r7.claim: Al-Wālibī transmits a similar interpretation from Ibn ʿAbbās: do not forget the work one does for the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r7.anchor: ونحو هذا روى الوالبي عن ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r8.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r8.claim: A report from ʿAlī says to use health, youth, and wealth to seek the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r8.anchor: وهو معنى ما روي عن علي: لا تنس صحتك وشبابك وغناك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid, through Ibn Abī Najīḥ, says obedience to God is one’s worldly share, for which one is rewarded in the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r9.anchor: روى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال: العمل بطاعة الله نصيبه من الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r10.claim: Qatāda interprets the share as lawful worldly provision and says to seek what is lawful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة: لا تنس الحلال من الدنيا؛ ابتغ الحلال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to take from one’s wealth only enough to live and devote the remainder to the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن: أمر أن يأخذ من ماله قدر عيشه، ويقدم ما سوى ذلك لآخرته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r12.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan also phrases the advice as putting the surplus forward and retaining what suffices.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r12.anchor: وعنه أيضا في هذا المعنى: قدم الفضل، وأمسك ما يبلغك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r13.speaker: ابن زاذان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r13.claim: A similar interpretation is transmitted from Ibn Zādhān: keep enough to live and reserve the rest for the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p456#2/r13.anchor: ونحو هذا روي عن ابن زاذان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the command to do good as obeying and worshipping God in response to His blessing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أطع الله واعبده كما أنعم عليك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r2.claim: Muqātil says to give generously in charity and good works as God has shown generosity, and not to use His gifts for sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: وأحسن العطية في الصدقة والخير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets seeking corruption in the land as inviting people to worship someone other than God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p458/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: {ولا تبغ الفساد في الأرض} فتدعو إلى عبادة غير الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r1.claim: Seek the Hereafter by spending the wealth God gave you in ways that please Him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r1.anchor: اطلبها بإنفاق مالك في رضا الله تعالى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r2.claim: Do not neglect to work in worldly life for the sake of your Hereafter.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r2.anchor: لا تترك أن تعمل في دنياك لآخرتك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:77-78/r3.claim: Do good to other people as God has done good to you.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r19.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r19.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r19.claim: Qārūn is urged to seek the hereafter through the blessings and hoards God gave him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p607/r19.anchor: } وابتغ فيما آتاك الله { [القصص: 77] من هذه النعم والخزائن.

ELMALILI:28:77-82/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r1.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r1.claim: Some take one's worldly share to mean lawful provision and legitimate worldly enjoyment; Elmalılı rejects that interpretation.
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r1.anchor: bazıları helâl dünya rızkı ve meşrû dünya zevki diye anlamak istemişlerse de

ELMALILI:28:77-82/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r2.claim: The phrase means the transient world; one's true share from it is benefit and deeds carried into the afterlife, as the world is the afterlife's cultivation.
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r2.anchor: o geçici dünyanın kendisi demektir. Asıl dünyadan nasib ise

ELMALILI:28:77-82/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r3.claim: He adds that worldly share ultimately amounts only to a shroud, illustrating this with Persian verse about people striving for a shroud between nonexistence and existence.
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r3.anchor: Yoksa dünyadan nasib nihâyet bir kefendir:

ELMALILI:28:77-82/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r4.claim: Hoarding such a great treasure and trapping wealth is itself corruption.
ELMALILI:28:77-82/r4.anchor: bu kadar hazineyi ihtikâr edip de serveti hapsetmek haddizâtında bir fesaddır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r4.claim: The counsel comes from believers enlightened through faith in God and His prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r4.anchor: 77. âyetteki öğüt, Allah’a ve peygamberine iman ederek aydınlanmış müminlerin öğüdüdür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r5.claim: One reading says the afterlife is the main aim while one may also lawfully enjoy the good things of this world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r5.anchor: Asıl amaç âhiret yurdunu kazanmaktır, ancak dünya nimetlerinden de meşru şekilde yararlanmak gerekir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r6.claim: The contextually stronger reading is that worldly life is brief, so one must not live as if it were eternal but use it in pursuit of the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:76/r6.anchor: Bağlama daha uygun olan açıklama ise şöyledir: Dünya hayatı, ebedî âlemdeki hayata göre çok kısadır

BAQILLANI:v1p193/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r4.claim: Five semantically distant clauses in the counsel to Qārūn are made more harmonious by their arrangement than phrases naturally associated from the outset.
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r4.anchor: وهي خمس كلمات متباعدة في المواقع نائية المطارح قد جعلها النظم البديع أشد تألفا

BAQILLANI:v1p193/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r5.claim: The author compares the counsel's cohesion with similarly composed passages about God's choice and the ruined town, where the clauses fit together unusually well.
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r5.anchor: ومثل هذه الآية قوله ( ﴿ وربك يخلق ما يشاء

BAQILLANI:v1p193/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r8.claim: Quranic story passages compress narratives together with admonitions, proverbs, wisdom, proofs of oneness, and declarations of God's transcendence; expanded prose would be heavier and less coherent.
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r8.anchor: كل سورة من هذه السور تتضمن من القصص ما لو تكلفت العبارة عنها بأضعاف كلماتها لم تستوف ما استوفت

BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r1.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r1.claim: The Prophet urges listeners to understand his teaching and transmit it; a bearer of religious knowledge may not understand it, while its recipient may understand more deeply.
BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r1.anchor: وروى زيد بن ثابت أن النبي خطب بالخيف من منى فقال نضر الله عبدا سمع مقالتي فوعاها

BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r2.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says believers' hearts remain sound through sincerity to God, sincere counsel to those in authority, and adherence to the community.
BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r2.anchor: ثلاث لا يغل عليهن قلب المؤمن إخلاص العمل لله والنصيحة لأولي الأمر ولزوم الجماعة

BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r3.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r3.claim: Those focused on the hereafter gain inner sufficiency and an ordered life while worldly goods come to them; those focused on this world face disorder and poverty and receive only what was decreed.
BAQILLANI:v1p132#2/r3.anchor: ومن كان همه الآخرة جمع الله شمله وجعل غناه في قلبه وأتته الدنيا وهي راغمة

BAQILLANI:v1p133/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p133/r1.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p133/r1.claim: The Prophet describes worldly life as attractive but temporary, says people are entrusted with it to be tested, and warns against worldly attachment and women.
BAQILLANI:v1p133/r1.anchor: رواها أبو سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال خطب بعد العصر فقال ألا إن الدنيا خضرة حلوة

BAQILLANI:v1p133/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p133/r2.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p133/r2.claim: He says fear of other people must not stop someone from speaking the truth once they know it.
BAQILLANI:v1p133/r2.anchor: ألا لا يمنعن رجلا مخافة الناس أن يقول الحق إذا علمه

BAQILLANI:v1p133/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p133/r3.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p133/r3.claim: At sunset he compares the short remainder of worldly life to the small part of that day still remaining.
BAQILLANI:v1p133/r3.anchor: إنه لم يبق من الدنيا فيما مضى إلا كما بقي من يومكم هذا فيما مضى

BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r1.speaker: علي
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r1.claim: ʿAlī portrays the world as departing and the hereafter as approaching: present life is a period of preparation before the contest, and using it well brings success.
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r1.anchor: أما بعد فإن الدنيا قد أدبرت وآذنت بوداع وإن الآخرة قد أقبلت وأشرفت باطلاع وإن المضمار اليوم

BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r2.speaker: علي
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r2.claim: He urges working for God in hope as in fear, warns that truth benefits while falsehood harms, and says failure to follow guidance lets error lead.
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r2.anchor: ألا فاعملوا لله في الرغبة كما تعملون له في الرهبة ألا وإني لم أر كالجنة نام طالبها

BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r3.speaker: علي
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r3.claim: People are commanded to depart and shown their provisions; his greatest fear for them is following desire and prolonging hope.
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r3.anchor: ألا وإنكم قد أمرتم بالظعن ودللتم على الزاد ألا وإن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم اتباع الهوى وطول الأمل

BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r4.speaker: علي
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r4.claim: In another sermon he says people were not created in vain and that worldly gains cannot replace the hereafter or outweigh what is lost there.
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r4.anchor: فما خلق امرؤ عبثا فيلهو ولا أهمل سدى فيلغو ما دنياه التي تحسنت إليه بخلف من الآخرة

BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r5.speaker: علي
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r5.claim: In a letter to Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAlī says joy and grief over worldly gains are misplaced; one should rejoice in good deeds, regret neglected duties, and focus on what follows death.
BAQILLANI:v1p145#2/r5.anchor: وكتب علي رضي الله عنه إلى عبد الله بن عباس رحمة الله عليهما وهو بالبصرة أما بعد فان المرء يسر بدرك

QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r1.claim: Qarun was being swallowed at Moses’ prayer; though Qarun appealed to their kinship, Moses kept telling the earth to take him, and Qarun never called directly on God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r1.anchor: وفيما أوحى الله إلى موسى : لقد ناداك بحق القرابة وأنت تقول : يا أرض خذيه

QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r2.claim: A story says that when Jonah was held in the fish, God made the fish circle the seas with him until he reached Qarun; God then ordered that Qarun’s sinking not be increased because he had asked about his cousin Moses and maintained kinship.
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r2.anchor: فلما حبس الله يونس في بطن الحوت أمر الحوت أن يطوف به في البحار لئلا يضيق قلب يونس

QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r3.claim: Admonition cannot benefit someone denied acceptance, just as seed cannot grow in saline ground; this explains why Qarun did not benefit from their advice.
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r3.anchor: وعظ من حرم القبول كمثل البذر في الأرض السبخة ؛ ولذا لم ينفعه نصحهم إياه

QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r4.claim: A person’s share of this world is neither to amass it all nor to renounce it all, but to take what benefits without later regret or punishment in the next life.
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r4.anchor: ليس النصيب من الدنيا جمعها ولا منعها ، إنما النصيب منها ما تكون فيه فائدة بحيث لا يعقب ندما

QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r5.claim: An inward reading makes worldly provisions a means to obey God with the self, know Him in the heart, remember Him with the tongue, and witness Him inwardly.
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r5.anchor: ويقال النصيب من الدنيا ما يحمل على طاعته بالنفس ، وعلى معرفته بالقلب ، وعلى ذكره باللسان ، وعلى مشاهدته بالسر

QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r6.claim: Qarun could only have done good had he believed, since an unbeliever has no good deed in this sense.
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r6.anchor: إنما كان يكون منه حسنة لو آمن بالله ؛ لأن الكافر لا حسنة له

QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r7.claim: The verse indicates that God grants worldly blessings even to an unbeliever.
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r7.anchor: والآية تدل على أن لله على الكافر نعما دنيوية

QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r8.claim: The commanded generosity is to spend blessings in obedience and service and answer them with gratitude rather than ingratitude.
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r8.anchor: والإحسان الذي أمر به إنفاق النعمة في وجوه الطاعة والخدمة ، ومقابلته بالشكران لا بالكفران

QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r9.claim: Another inward sense of doing good is recognizing divine favor without imagining that one deserves it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p446/r9.anchor: ويقال الإحسان رؤية الفضل دون توهم الاستحقاق

BURHAN:v4p6/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p6/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p6/r1.claim: Earth is usually singular because it denotes the lower realm, a quality opposed to height, rather than a count of discrete entities.
BURHAN:v4p6/r1.anchor: أنها بمنزلة السفل والتحت ولكن وصف بها هذا المكان المحسوس فجرت مجرى امرأة زور وضيف فلا معنى لجمعهما

BURHAN:v4p6/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p6/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v4p6/r2.claim: The hadith about one who wrongfully takes land treats the seven earths as distinct, countable tracts, permitting the plural when parcels are specified.
BURHAN:v4p6/r2.anchor: ومنه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم طوقه من سبع أرضين فجمعها لما اعتمد الكلام على ذات الأرض

BURHAN:v4p6/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p6/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p6/r3.claim: The heavens are plural because their entities, rather than the quality of height, are meant; their small number suits the sound plural, unlike earth as lower realm.
BURHAN:v4p6/r3.anchor: وأما جمع السموات فإن المقصود بها ذاتها دون معنى الوصف فلهذا جمعت جمع سلامة لأن العدد قليل

BURHAN:v4p6/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p6/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p6/r4.claim: Earth remains a collective singular beside the heavens because, even if multiple, it is like one small pebble compared with a desert.
BURHAN:v4p6/r4.anchor: بل هي بالنسبة إليها كحصاة في صحراء فهي وإن تعددت كالواحد القليل

BURHAN:v4p6/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p6/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p6/r5.claim: Earth is the abode of this world, which revelation diminishes by comparing it with the hereafter; on one view the heavens are not part of this world.
BURHAN:v4p6/r5.anchor: كما يدخل الإنسان إصبعه في اليم فما يلعق بها هو مثال الدنيا

BURHAN:v4p6/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p6/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p6/r6.claim: When heaven means the encompassing quality of above or height, it is singular, like earth, rather than a particular heaven.
BURHAN:v4p6/r6.anchor: فإذا أريد الوصف الشامل للسموات وهو معنى العلو والفوق أفردته كالأرض بدليل قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v4p6/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p6/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p6/r7.claim: The singular السماء in 10:61 reflects the comprehensive quality of height; 34:3 uses plural السماوات because context stresses God's knowledge of all His dominion.
BURHAN:v4p6/r7.anchor: وأن له ما في السموات وما في الأرض فاقتضى السياق أن يذكر سعة علمه

SULAMI:v2p109#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r1.claim: Abū ʿUthmān says that failing to make the world serve the afterlife and the afterlife lead to God wastes one’s effort and nullifies one’s work.
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : من لم يجعل حظه من دنياه آخرته ومن آخرته ربه فقد خاب سعيه ، وبطل عمله

SULAMI:v2p109#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r2.claim: He defines a servant’s worldly share as guarding God’s and His friends’ sanctities and showing compassion to His servants.
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r2.anchor: ونصيب العبد من دنياه حفظ حرمات الله وحرمة أوليائه والشفقة على عامة أوليائه وعباده

SULAMI:v2p109#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r3.claim: Another view is that one should take only enough wealth for a livelihood and direct the rest toward the afterlife.
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : أمره أن يأخذ من ماله قدر عيشه وإن تقدم ما سوى ذلك لآخرته

SULAMI:v2p109#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r4.speaker: سفيان الثوري
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r4.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī says not to neglect one’s lifetime in this world, but to use it for obedience.
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r4.anchor: وسئل سفيان الثوري رحمة الله عليه عن قوله : ﴿ ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا ﴾ قال : لا تغفل عن عمرك في الدنيا أن تعمل بالطاعة

SULAMI:v2p109#5/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r5.claim: Another view defines one’s share as avoiding delusion by the world and refusing to settle into it, since it endures for no one.
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : نصيبك منها أن لا تغتر بها ولا تسكن إليها فإنها لم تدم لأحد ولم تبق له

SULAMI:v2p109#5/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r6.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r6.claim: Al-Junayd says not to abandon sincerity to God in worldly action, since it brings one near to Him and cuts one off from all else.
SULAMI:v2p109#5/r6.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه في هذه الآية : لا تترك إخلاص العمل لله في الدنيا فهو الذي يقربك منه ويقطعك عما سواه

SULAMI:v2p110/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p110/r1.speaker: القيم
SULAMI:v2p110/r1.claim: Al-Qayyim urges turning wholly toward God, honoring the knowledge of Him, and responding to His gifts of faith and service with sincere, dutiful worship.
SULAMI:v2p110/r1.anchor: قال القيم : اصرف وجهك عن الكل بالإقبال عليه كما احسن الله إليك حيث جعلك من أهل معرفته

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r1.claim: لا is a particle of negation and may also function with the sense of لم, as shown by a cited poetic line.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r1.anchor: ' لا ' حرف موضوع للنفي . وقد يكون بمعنى ' لم ' وأنشدوا من ذلك :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r3.claim: A second use is prohibition, including the command not to forget one's share of worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p631#2/r3.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن ' لا ' في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r1.claim: Few has no fixed measure in itself; it is understood relative to something else, just as many is.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r1.anchor: القليل : لا حد له في نفسه . وإنما يعرف بالإضافة إلى غيره . مثله الكثير

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r2.claim: The entry says that when usury grows, it is ultimately headed toward diminution.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r2.anchor: وفي ذكر الربا إن كثر فإنه إلى قل .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r3.claim: The expression فلان قل بن قل describes someone whose identity and father's identity are both unknown.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r3.anchor: ( وفلان قل بن قل ) : إذا كان لا يعرف هو ولا أبوه .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r4.claim: القلة can be the amount a person lifts from a jar or similar vessel; linguists set no fixed limit, and the entry cites a poem about drinking from pitchers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r4.anchor: والقلة : ما أقله الإنسان من جرة أو نحوها . وليس في ذلك عند أهل اللغة حد محدود .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r5.claim: القلة also names a mountain peak, while استقل القوم means that the people went on their way.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p492/r5.anchor: والقلة : قلة الجبل . واستقل القوم : مضوا لسبيلهم .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335/r1.claim: The instruction means do not leave your share of worldly life.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p335/r1.anchor: {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} أي لا تترك حظك منها.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r2.claim: In the hadith comparing people to a hundred camels, the hundred means a herd gathered at pasture and is also called hunayda; a riding camel stands out by maturity and appearance.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r2.anchor: الإبل المائة: هي الراعية، وإنما يجتمع منها في المرعى الواحد مائة، فتقام المائة مقام القطيع

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r3.claim: The camel comparison means people are equal under law and in retaliation; rank gives no one an advantage. The author links it with the comb-teeth saying and an Arab donkey-teeth proverb.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r3.anchor: فأراد: أنهم سواء في الأحكام وفي القصاص، ليس لشريف فضل على غيره

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r4.claim: Ḥabaṭ is a camel's belly swelling after it eats too much pasture; yulam means that it nearly kills.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r4.anchor: فالحبط: أن تأكل الناقة في المرعي فتكثر حتى تنتفخ بطنها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r5.claim: The Prophet's warning about spring growth illustrates avoiding excess worldly abundance and beauty when they can prove destructive, like an animal overeating grass.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r5.anchor: وإنما نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الاستكثار من الدنيا ومن غضارتها وحسنها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r6.claim: The instruction to settle in a house like a gazelle means to stay quietly without doing anything, like a gazelle settled in its lair.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r6.anchor: يراد: أقم ولا تحدث شيئا كأنك ظبي قد استقر في الكناس

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r7.claim: “Clothed yet naked” women are those wearing thin garments that do not cover them.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r7.anchor: يعني النساء اللواتي يلبسن رقاق الثياب، فهن كاسيات إذا لبسن، عاريات إذا كن لا يسترهن

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r8.claim: In a peace document, a “closed bag” means a heart clear of rancor and committed to fidelity; Arabs call the chests ʿiyāb, as an unnamed poet confirms.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p302#6/r8.anchor: يريد: صدرا نقيا من الغل والعداوة، منطويا على الوفاء

MAJAZ:v2p111/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p111/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p111/r2.claim: Do not forget your share of this world means do not abandon your portion or lawful pursuit of provision.
MAJAZ:v2p111/r2.anchor: «ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا» (77) مجازه: لا تدع حظك وطلب الرزق الحلال منها

SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r1.claim: فيمآ آتاك depends on ابتغ or an omitted circumstantial phrase meaning moving about among God's gifts.
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق ب " ابتغ " ، وأن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال أي: متقلبا فيما آتاك.

SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r2.claim: ما is a verbal-noun particle or means that which.
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r2.anchor: و " ما " مصدرية أو بمعنى الذي.

SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r3.claim: It means kindness like God's kindness to you.

SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r4.claim: في الأرض depends on تبغ, الفساد, or an omitted circumstantial phrase, the last being remote.
SAMIN-DURR:28:77/r4.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق ب " تبغ " أو بالفساد، أو بمحذوف على أنه حال وهو بعيد.

ASAD-NOTES:28:77#n86/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:77#n86/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:77#n86/r1.claim: Seeking the hereafter through God's gifts means spending in charity and on good causes.
ASAD-NOTES:28:77#n86/r1.anchor: I.e., by spending in charity and on good causes.

ASAD-NOTES:28:77#n87/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:77#n87/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:77#n87/r1.claim: The call not to neglect one's share in worldly life asks for generosity balanced by moderation.
ASAD-NOTES:28:77#n87/r1.anchor: a call to generosity and, at the same time, to moderation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r1.claim: Verse 77 further details the learned men’s advice to Qārūn, with each sentence offering wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r1.anchor: Each and every sentence of it is a treasure of wisdom and sagacity.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r2.claim: Wealth is God’s gift, not inherited property or the product of one’s own ability; it tests whether a person serves wealth or uses it to seek God’s pleasure and the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r2.anchor: They were purely a blessing f rom God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r3.claim: The world is mortal; only what one spends for God’s cause benefits eternal life, while neglecting God’s and creatures’ rights and becoming enslaved to wealth leads to ruin.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r3.anchor: Only that will benefit them in their everlasting lives which today they spend for God’s cause.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r4.speaker: Our exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r4.claim: The common interpretation is that one should not neglect one’s worldly share, meaning one need not abandon the world for the Hereafter; Islahi rejects this reading as incorrect.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r4.anchor: Our exegetes have generally interpreted these words to mean

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r5.claim: As God has been gracious to people, they should be gracious to others; God wants His attributes reflected in His creatures and dislikes miserliness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r5.anchor: the God Who is munificent with His people does not like people who are miserly with others.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r6.claim: Fasād is not merely theft and robbery, which are outward manifestations; its true core is arrogance, overstepping worship’s bounds and violating God’s rights and sacred limits.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r6.anchor: It does not merely connote theft and robbery

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p571/r7.claim: Those who spread such disorder are people God dislikes, like unwanted weeds and self-invited guests in His orchard, destined to be uprooted and displaced.

NASHR:v1p180/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p180/r1.speaker: ابن يونس
NASHR:v1p180/r1.claim: Ibn al-Naffākh died in Egypt in 314 AH; Ibn Yūnus describes him as trustworthy and firm, a hadith scholar who lived simply.
NASHR:v1p180/r1.anchor: وتوفي ابن النفاخ) سنة أربع عشرة وثلاثمائة بمصر، وكان ثقة مشهورا صالحا، قال ابن يونس:

NASHR:v1p180/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p180/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p180/r2.claim: Ibn Nahshal died in 294 AH and was an accomplished, precise, virtuous recitation imam who served as imam of Isfahan’s mosque.
NASHR:v1p180/r2.anchor: وتوفي ابن نهشل) سنة أربع وتسعين ومائتين، وكان إماما في القراءة مجودا فاضلا ضابطا،

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r1.claim: Qatāda says not to forget one’s portion of this world means to pursue what is lawful in worldly life.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا ﴾ قال لا تنسى الحلال من الدنيا أي اتبع الحلال

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r2.claim: Mujāhid says one’s worldly portion is acting in obedience to God, for which one is rewarded in the hereafter.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا ﴾ قال العمل بطاعة الله نصيبه من الدنيا الذي يثاب عليه في الآخرة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Qarun was instructed to take enough for his needs and leave what exceeded that.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p93/r3.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا ﴾ قال أمره أن يأخذ قدر قوته ويدع ما سوى ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r1.claim: The wealth and riches God gave Qarun should be directed toward the hereafter's reward by spending them on means that lead to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r1.anchor: أي ثوابها أي ثواب الله تعالى فيها بصرف ذلك إلى ما يكون وسيلة اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r2.claim: The preposition في can be locative: pursue the hereafter while moving and acting within the wealth God gave.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r2.anchor: إما ظرفية على معنى ابتغ متقلبا ومتصرفا فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, في is causal: pursue the hereafter by spending what God has given you.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r3.anchor: أو سببية على معنى ابتغ بصرف ما أتاك الله تعالى ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r4.claim: A reading is اتبع instead of وابتغ.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains one's worldly share as working in this life for the hereafter.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن تعمل فيها لآخرتك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r6.claim: Mujahid is also reported to explain the share as acting in this life for the hereafter.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r6.anchor: وروي ذلك عن مجاهد وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r7.claim: Qatada says to take from worldly life what God has made lawful.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة هو أن تأخذ من الدنيا ما أحل الله تعالى لك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r8.speaker: منصور
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r8.claim: Mansur says the share is not worldly property but one's lifetime, in which one should send deeds ahead for the hereafter.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r8.anchor: ليس هو عرض الدنيا ولكن نصيبك عمرك

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan advises giving away the surplus while keeping what is enough to live on.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r10.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r10.claim: Malik interprets the worldly share as eating and drinking without extravagance.

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r11.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r11.claim: An anonymous poet suggests that one's whole worldly share is only two shrouds and burial perfume.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r11.anchor: نصيبك مما تجمع الدهر كله رداءان تلوى فيهما وحنوط

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r12.claim: The warning strongly urges Qarun to prepare for the afterlife from his wealth: if only a shroud remains as one's share, one should advance what benefits one there.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r12.anchor: وفي نهيهم إياه عن نسيان ذلك حض عظيم له على التزود من ماله للآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r13.claim: Do good to God's servants as God has done good to you, either by analogy with His kindness or because He favored you.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r13.anchor: أي مثل إحسانه تعالى فيما أنعم به عليك والتشبيه في مطلق الاحسان

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r14.claim: The كاف can mark comparison or causation, meaning do good because of God's kindness to you.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r14.anchor: أو لأجل إحسانه سبحانه إليك على أن الكاف للتعليل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r15.claim: Another explanation is to do good through gratitude and obedience, as God did good by granting blessings.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r15.anchor: وأحسن بالشكر والطاعة كما أحسن الله تعالى عليك بالانعام

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r16.claim: The prohibition tells Qarun to stop persisting in the oppression and transgression he has been practicing.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r16.anchor: نهي عن الاستمرار على ما هو عليه من الظلم والبغي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r17.claim: Al-Alusi says this closing clause is explained as in the parallel wording about God not loving the arrogant rejoicers.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r17.anchor: قوله سبحانه : ( إن الله لايحب الفرحين )

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r18.claim: Al-Alusi takes the whole admonition as spoken by believers among Qarun's people, as the verse apparently indicates.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r18.anchor: هذه الموعظة بأسرها كانت من مؤمني قومه كما هو ظاهر اة ية

ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r19.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r19.claim: An alternative view says that Moses delivered the whole admonition.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p112#2/r19.anchor: إنها كانت من موسى عليه السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r1.claim: Use the wealth and blessings God gave to seek the afterlife by thanking Him and spending in what pleases Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r1.anchor: اطلب فيما أعطاك الله من الأموال والنعمة والجنة وهو أن تقوم بشكر الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd say not to abandon worldly work for the afterlife, since a person’s true worldly share is working for the afterlife and escape from punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد، وابن زيد: لا تترك أن تعمل في الدنيا للآخرة حتى تنجو من العذاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the worldly share as almsgiving and maintaining kinship.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r4.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r4.claim: ʿAlī says to use health, strength, youth, and wealth to seek the afterlife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r4.anchor: وقال علي: لا تنس صحتك وقوتك وشبابك وغناك أن تطلب بها الآخرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r5.claim: Amr ibn Maymūn al-Awdī reports the Prophet advising a man to seize five before five: youth before old age, health before illness, wealth before poverty, free time before busyness, and life before death; Baghawī calls the report mursal.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r5.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون الأودي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لرجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says one should give the surplus while keeping what suffices.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r6.anchor: قال الحسن: أمر أن يقدم الفضل ويمسك ما يغنيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r7.speaker: منصور بن زاذان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r7.claim: Manṣūr ibn Zādhān says a person’s share of this world is provision for oneself and one’s family.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#2/r7.anchor: قال منصور بن زاذان في قوله:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r1.claim: The instruction means to do good through obedience to God, as God has done good through His blessings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r1.anchor: [أي: أحسن بطاعة الله] (3) كما أحسن الله إليك بنعمته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r2.claim: Another reported explanation says to do good to the Fire as God has done good to you.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: أحسن إلى النار كما أحسن الله إليك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r3.claim: Anyone who disobeys God has sought corruption in the earth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p221#3/r3.anchor: من عصى الله فقد طلب الفساد في الأرض

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r1.claim: Use the wealth God gave you to seek the afterlife, spending it on what secures it; wealth is meant as a means to the next life.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r1.anchor: بصرفه فيما يوجبها لك فإن المقصود منه أن يكون وصلة إليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r2.claim: Do not neglect your share of this world: use it to attain the afterlife and take what suffices for you.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r2.anchor: ولا تترك ترك المنسي. { نصيبك من الدنيا } وهو أن تحصل بها آخرتك

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r3.claim: Do good to God's servants as God has shown goodness to you.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r3.anchor: إلى عباد الله. { كما أحسن الله إليك } فيما أنعم الله عليك

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r4.claim: Another interpretation is to do good through gratitude and obedience, as God did good through His gifts.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r4.anchor: وقيل { أحسن } بالشكر والطاعة { كما أحسن } إليك بالإنعام

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r5.claim: Do not cause corruption by any act that leads to injustice or transgression; the command rebukes Qarun's prior wrongdoing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r5.anchor: بأمر يكون علة للظلم والبغي، نهي له عما كان عليه من الظلم والبغي

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:77-78/r6.claim: God does not love corrupters because of their evil actions.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.claim: After the partners’ helplessness in the Hereafter, the text shows God’s rule in this world by destroying arrogant people who cannot save one another.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r1.anchor: ولما دل على عجزهم في تلك الدار , وعلمهم أن المتصرف في جميع الأقدار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r5.claim: Those who boast in gifts must recognize God’s right in what the messengers and scriptures teach; worldly possessions cannot save those who rely on them as if they secured lasting happiness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r5.anchor: أن الحق لله في كل ما دعت إليه رسله , ونطقت به كتبه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r6.claim: Their worldly dependence resembles the spider that takes a house, a comparison found in the following sūra.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p516/r6.anchor: كما يأتي في التي بعده كمثل العنكبوت اتخذت بيتا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r6.claim: The text implies an additional call to renounce worldly attachment because abstaining from this joy leads to asceticism and nearness to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r6.anchor: ترك الفرح سببا للزهد , وهو سبب القرب إلى الله , كان كأن قيل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r7.claim: Ibtaghi commands Qarun to seek with strenuous effort.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r7.anchor: أي اطلب طلبا تجهد نفسك فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r8.claim: He should use God’s wealth to pursue the Hereafter by spending it in ways God loves; this pursuit gives wealth life and reminds him that the world is temporary and all its possessions perish.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r8.anchor: أي الملك الأعظم الذي له الأمر كله من هذه الأموال حال تمكنك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r9.claim: He may enjoy lawful food, clothing, marriage, and homes, but without excess or vanity that abandons fairness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r9.anchor: بل استعمل المباحات من المآكل والملابس والمناكح والمساكن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r10.speaker: علي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r10.claim: Ali explains one’s worldly share as health, strength, vitality, and wealth that can be used to seek the Hereafter.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r10.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه : ولا تنس صحتك وقوتك ونشاطك وغناك أن تطلب به الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r11.claim: Because human appetite grows once a little worldly enjoyment is allowed, Qarun’s people add further counsel to restrain his greed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518/r11.anchor: فإذا أذن لها من الدنيا في نقير جعلته أكبر كبير

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r1.claim: The command to do good means giving wealth to the needy and spending in every form of obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r1.anchor: أي أوقع الإحسان بدفع المال إلى المحاويج

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r2.claim: Give as God has given to you, with the liberality of one who does not fear poverty, since God made you prosperous.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r2.anchor: بأن تعطي عطاء من لا يخاف الفقر كما أوسع عليك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r3.claim: Corruption includes miserliness or extravagance, arrogance toward God's servants, and belittling them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r3.anchor: ولا تبذير , ولا تكبر على عباد الله ولا تحقير

BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r4.claim: God's lack of love means He does not treat corrupters as beloved or honor them; this corrects the assumption that worldly prosperity signals divine favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p518#2/r4.anchor: أكثر المفسدين يبسط لهم في الدنيا , وأكثرالناس يستبعد

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r3.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says to seek the Hereafter by giving charity, drawing near to God, and maintaining kinship ties.
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r3.anchor: قال: إن الله لا يحب بطرا {وابتغ فيما آتاك الله الدار الآخرة} قال: تصدق وتقرب إلى الله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that one must not abandon working for God during worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r4.anchor:
عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {إن الله لا يحب الفرحين} قال: المرحين
وفي قوله {وابتغ فيما آتاك الله

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r5.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas says the worldly share is to work in this life for the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} قال: أن تعمل فيها لآخرتك

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies one's worldly share as obedience to God, for which one is rewarded in the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} قال: العمل بطاعة الله نصيبه من الدنيا الذي يثاب عليه في الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r7.claim: Al-Hasan advises giving away one's surplus while retaining enough to live; another wording says to keep a year's provisions and give the rest in charity.
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r7.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {ولا تنس نصيبك} قال: قدم الفضل وأمسك ما يبلغك - وفي لفظ - قال: امسك قوت سنة وتصدق بما بقي

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r8.claim: Qatada says to take from this world what God has made lawful, which provides sufficiency.
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} قال: أن تأخذ من الدنيا ما أحل الله لك فإن لك فيه غنى وكفاية

DURR-FULL:v6p439/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r9.speaker: منصور
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r9.claim: Mansur says the worldly share is not worldly goods but one's lifetime, in which one should prepare for the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v6p439/r9.anchor: عن منصور رضي الله عنه في قوله {ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا} قال: ليس هو عرض من عرض الدنيا ولكن هو نصيبك عمرك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r1.claim: Al-Suddī explains seeking the afterlife through charity, drawing near to God, and maintaining kinship ties.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r1.anchor: به ، عن السدي وابتغ فيما اتاك الله الدار الاخرة قال : تصدق ، وقرب إلى الله تبارك وتعالى ، وصل الرحم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says one’s worldly share is to work in this life for the afterlife.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا قال : ان تعمل فيها لاخرتك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says not to forget doing God’s work in this world.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا يقول : لا تترك ان تعمل لله في الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r4.claim: Mujāhid says to work in this life in obedience to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا قال : ان تعمل فيها بطاعتي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r5.claim: Mujāhid identifies one’s worldly share as one’s lifetime, in which to work for the afterlife.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا قال : عمرك تعمل فيه لاخرتك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to give away surplus wealth while retaining enough for one’s needs.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r6.anchor: عن الحسن ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا قال : اعط الفضل وامسك ما يبلغك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan also says to take from one’s wealth only what is enough to live on.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r7.anchor: سالت الحسن ، عن هذه الاية ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا قال : امره ان ياخذ من ماله قدر عيشه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r8.claim: Qatāda says to be content with what God has made lawful for you.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا قال : استغن بما احل الله لك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r9.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says not to forget sending worldly wealth ahead for the afterlife, since there one finds only what one sent ahead from God’s provision.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r9.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قول الله : ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا قال : لا تنس ان تقدم من دنياك لاخرتك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r10.speaker: مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r10.claim: When asked its meaning, Mālik says one may live, eat, and drink without being unduly constrained.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3010/r10.anchor: سئل مالك ، ما هو ؟ قال : ان يعيش وياكل ويشرب غير مضيق عليه في راي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to retain enough wealth for one’s living and direct whatever exceeds it toward the afterlife.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r1.anchor: سالت الحسن ، عن هذه الاية ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا واحسن كما احسن الله اليك قال : امره ان ياخذ من ماله قدر عيشته

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to keep a year’s subsistence and give the rest in charity.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا واحسن كما احسن الله اليك قال : احبس قوت سنة ، وتصدق بما بقي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, as transmitted by Qatāda, says to take what God has made lawful, which provides sufficiency.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ، عن الحسن ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا واحسن كما احسن الله اليك قال : اي ما احل الله لك منها ، فان لك فيها غنى وكفاية

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
