IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd explains doing good as using well what God has increased or granted you.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r4.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قوله : واحسن كما احسن الله اليك يقول : احسن فيما زادك الله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r5.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib identifies clipping or cutting gold and silver as corruption in the land.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r5.anchor: عن يحيى بن سعيد انه سمع سعيد بن المسيب يقول : قطع الذهب والورق من الفساد في الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r6.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r6.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna glosses God’s not loving corrupters with the phrase لا يقرب.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r6.anchor: عن أبيه أو عمه سفيان ابن عيينة قوله : ان الله لا يحب المفسدين لا يقرب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God does not love or approve the practice of corruption.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3011/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس ان الله لا يحب الفساد اي لا يحب عمله ولا يرضاه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r8.claim: Seeking the afterlife means seeking its bliss and reward.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r9.claim: The ظرفية in فيما آتاك الله is figurative: Qarun should use the greater part of God’s gifts, his treasure, to seek the afterlife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r9.anchor: وعلق بفعل الابتغاء قوله { فيما ءاتاك الله } بحرف الظرفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r10.claim: The figurative sense is like رزقوهم فيها واكسوهم in 4:5, meaning give them from it and from its greater portion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p177#2/r10.anchor: فالظرفية هنا كالتي في قوله تعالى { وارزقوهم فيها واكسوهم } ( النساء : 5 ) أي منها ومعظمها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r1.claim: The poetic example supports figurative ظرفية: seek reward by spending Qarun’s treasures in God’s way and in the required and encouraged acts of charity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r2.claim: Qarun is urged to gain reward by giving from his treasures for God’s cause, obligatory duties, and recommended charitable works.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r2.anchor: أي اطلب بكنوزك أسباب حصول الثواب بالإنفاق منها في سبيل الله وما أوجبه ورغب فيه من القربان ووجوه البر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r3.claim: The sentence is parenthetical between the two surrounding clauses, and its waw is parenthetical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r3.anchor: جملة معترضة بين الجملتين الحافتين بها ، والواو اعتراضية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r4.claim: The prohibition is permissive, and forgetfulness figuratively means neglect: Qarun may take a worldly share that does not consume his share of the afterlife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r4.anchor: والنهي في { ولا تنس نصيبك } مستعمل في الإباحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r5.claim: This qualification softens the admonition so Qarun will not infer that he must devote all his wealth to worship and reject every worldly pleasure; he may enjoy some of it after paying God’s due.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r5.anchor: وهذا احتراس في الموعظة خشية نفور الموعوظ من موعظة الواعظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r6.claim: Naṣīb means a share or portion; the word derives from نصب because what is allotted to someone is set out and distinguished.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r6.anchor: والنصيب : الحظ والقسط ، وهو فعيل من النصب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r7.claim: The possessive نصيبك marks a personal right to use wealth for fitting worldly enjoyment, provided it is neither worship nor forbidden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r7.anchor: وإضافة النصيب إلى ضميره دالة على أنه حقه وأن للمرء الانتفاع بماله في ما يلائمه في الدنيا خاصة مما ليس من القربات ولم يكن حراما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r8.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r8.claim: Malik says the worldly share means living, eating, and drinking without undue restriction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r8.anchor: قال مالك : في رأيي معنى { ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r9.claim: Qatada says the worldly share is everything lawful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة : نصيب الدنيا هو الحلال كله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r10.claim: The verse exemplifies a prohibitive form used to convey permission; من is partitive, and الدنيا means worldly enjoyment, of which the person has a share.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r10.anchor: وبذلك تكون هذه الآية مثالا لاستعمال صيغة النهي لمعنى الإباحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r11.claim: Beneficence already falls under seeking the afterlife, but it is singled out to prepare the argument based on God’s beneficence to Qarun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r11.anchor: الإحسان داخل في عموم ابتغاء الدار الآخرة ولكنه ذكر هنا ليبنى عليه الاحتجاج بقوله { كما أحسن الله إليك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r12.claim: The kāf marks comparison and ما is a verbal noun: render beneficence like God’s beneficence; its causal force arises from comparison rather than being a separate meaning of kāf.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r13.claim: The likeness is that gratitude for each blessing should take a corresponding form; grammarians call the kāf causal, as in 2:198, but causality follows from comparison.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p178/r13.anchor: والتحقيق أن التعليل حاصل من معنى التشبيه وليس معنى مستقلا من معاني الكاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r1.claim: The object of أحسن is omitted to generalize beneficence toward oneself, one’s people, animals, and other creatures within one’s power to help.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r1.anchor: وحذف متعلق الإحسان لتعميم ما يحسن إليه فيشمل نفسه وقومه ودوابه ومخلوقات الله الداخلة في دائرة التمكن من الإحسان إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r2.claim: A hadith says God prescribed excellence in every thing; the author gives no grading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( إن الله كتب الإحسان على كل شيء )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r3.claim: Beneficence suits each recipient and situation, including keeping permitted harm to its measure and showing good speech, a welcoming face, and a pleasant manner.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r3.anchor: فالإحسان في كل شيء بحسبه ، والإحسان لكل شيء بما يناسبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r4.claim: The prohibition is added because doing good to some while harming others might be mistaken for overall beneficence; the explicit warning bars mixing good with corruption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r4.anchor: وعطف { لا تبغ الفساد في الأرض } للتحذير من خلط الإحسان بالفساد فإن الفساد ضد الإحسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r5.claim: The earth means the land where Qarun’s people live; since it is part of the globe, corruption there is corruption within the earth as a whole.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r5.anchor: والمراد بالأرض أرضهم التي هم حالون بها ، وإذ قد كانت جزءا من الكرة الأرضية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r6.claim: The wording has parallels including 2:205, where someone turns away and strives to corrupt the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r6.anchor: وقد تقدمت نظائره منها في قوله تعالى { وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها } في سورة البقرة ( 205 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r7.claim: God’s lack of love for corrupters explains the prohibition: servants may not do what God does not love.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r7.anchor: وجملة { إن الله لا يحب المفسدين } علة للنهي عن الإفساد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r8.claim: Qarun was a monotheist following Israel’s religion, but doubted Moses’ promises and prescriptions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p179/r8.anchor: وقد كان { قارون } موحدا على دين إسرائيل ولكنه كان شاكا في صدق مواعيد موسى وفي تشريعاته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r21.speaker: ابن عباس والجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r21.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most interpreters say not to forget one’s share means do good in this world, since the afterlife is earned here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r21.anchor: فقال ابن عباس والجمهور: معناه لا تضيع عمرك في أن لا تعمل عملا صالحا في دنياك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r22.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r22.claim: The people tell Qārūn to use his wealth to seek God’s pleasure and prepare for the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p298/r22.anchor: ثم وصوه أن يطلب بماله رضى الله تعالى ويقدم لآخرته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r1.claim: On Ibn ʿAbbās and the majority’s interpretation, the admonition is stern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r1.anchor: فالكلام كله على هذا التأويل شدة في الموعظة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatāda say to enjoy lawful things, pursue them, and consider worldly prospects.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: معناه ولا تضيع أيضا حظك من دنياك في تمتعك بالحلال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r3.claim: The author favors the gentler counsel to avoid alienating the person through harshness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r3.anchor: فالكلام على هذا التأويل فيه بعض الرفق به وإصلاح الأمر الذي يشتهيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says to give away the surplus and keep what suffices.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه قدم الفضل وأمسك ما يبلغ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r5.claim: Mālik says one’s share is eating and drinking without extravagance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r5.anchor: وقال مالك: هو الأكل والشرب بلا سرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r6.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r6.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī reports that the share meant one’s shroud; the author explains that one leaves all wealth except the burial cloth, also cited in poetry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r6.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي أنه قيل أرادوا بنصيبه الكفن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r7.claim: “Do good as God has done good to you” means charity to the poor and needy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p299/r7.anchor: وقوله وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك أمر بصلة المساكين وذوي الحاجة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r1.claim: Seek the afterlife through the wealth God gave you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r1.anchor: أي اطلب فيما أعطاك الله من الأموال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r2.speaker: أبو المتوكل وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r2.claim: Abu al-Mutawakkil and Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ read واتبع with doubled ta, kasra on ba, and a still undotted ayn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو المتوكل وابن السميفع واتبع بتشديد التاء وكسر الباء بعدها وعين ساكنة غير معجمة الدار الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and most commentators say to work in this world for the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r3.anchor: أحدها أن يعمل في الدنيا للآخرة قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says give the surplus and retain enough to live on.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r4.anchor: والثاني أن يقدم الفضل ويمسك ما يغنيه قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r5.claim: Qatada says lawful wealth should suffice, avoiding the forbidden.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r5.anchor: والثالث أن يستغني بالحلال عن الحرام قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r6.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r6.claim: One of al-Mawardi's views is to give surplus wealth, as God gave beyond your needs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r6.anchor: أحدها أعط فضل مالك كما زادك على قدر حاجتك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r7.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r7.claim: A second view is to do what God made obligatory, as He has bestowed blessings on you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r7.anchor: والثاني أحسن فيما افترض عليك كما أحسن في إنعامه إليك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r8.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r8.claim: A third view is to seek lawful provision as God made good things lawful for you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r8.anchor: والثالث أحسن في طلب الحلال كما أحسن إليك في الإحلال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p241/r9.claim: Seeking corruption means committing sins in the land.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r1.claim: Use the great wealth and blessing God gave you to obey Him and draw near through good deeds that earn reward in the next life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r1.anchor: استعمل ما وهبك الله من هذا المال الجزيل والنعمة الطائلة، في طاعة ربك والتقرب إليه بأنواع القربات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r2.claim: Enjoy what God permits of food, drink, clothing, housing, and marriage, while meeting the rights owed to God, oneself, family, and guests.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r2.anchor: مما أباح الله فيها (5) من المآكل والمشارب والملابس والمساكن والمناكح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r3.claim: Do good to God's creatures as God has done good to you.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r3.anchor: أحسن إلى خلقه كما أحسن هو إليك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r4.claim: Do not make corrupting the earth and harming God's creatures your aim while enjoying what you have.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p253#3/r4.anchor: لا تكن همتك بما أنت فيه أن تفسد به الأرض (1) ، وتسيء إلى خلق الله

JISHUMI:v8p5534/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5534/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5534/r1.claim: A person’s share of this world is what he spends in charitable good; what he keeps until death belongs to heirs.
JISHUMI:v8p5534/r1.anchor: وتدل أن نصيب المرء في دنياه ما أنفقه في وجوه البر، لا ما تمسك به حتى مات، فإن ذلك نصيب الورثة.

JISHUMI:v8p5534/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5534/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5534/r2.claim: Since God does not love corruption, He does not will it; if He created it, He would will it, refuting the Mujabbira account of creation and will.
JISHUMI:v8p5534/r2.anchor: ويدل قوله: (لا يحب المفسدين) أنه لا يريد الفساد، ولو كان خلقه لأراده، فيبطل قول المجبرة

JISHUMI:v8p5535/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5535/r3.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v8p5535/r3.claim: The Judge says the verse gathers religious and worldly concerns: “seek” covers all obligations, while “do not forget” covers the self’s desires, assuming it means what is rightfully due to oneself.
JISHUMI:v8p5535/r3.anchor: قال القاضي - رحمه الله -: قد جمع تعالى في قوله: (وابتغ فيما آتاك الله الدار الآخرة ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r3.claim: Use God-given wealth and abundance for the afterlife by doing obligatory and recommended good works and making it provision for that journey.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r3.anchor: من الغنى والثروة { الدار الاخرة } بأن تفعل فيه أفعال الخير من أصناف الواجب والمندوب إليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r4.claim: Your share of this world is what you take from your wealth to meet your needs and benefit you.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r4.anchor: ولا تنس نصيبك } وهو أن تأخذ منه ما يكفيك ويصلحك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r5.claim: One explanation is to do good to God’s servants as God has done good to you.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r5.anchor: وأحسن } إلى عباد الله { كما أحسن الله إليك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r6.claim: Another explanation is to show gratitude and obedience to God for His kindness to you.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r6.anchor: أوأحسن بشكرك وطاعتك لله كما أحسن إليك .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r7.claim: Corruption on earth here means the oppression and transgression Qārūn practiced.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r7.anchor: والفساد في الأرض : ما كان عليه من الظلم والبغي .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r8.claim: A reported view identifies Moses as the speaker of the exhortation to Qārūn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r8.anchor: وقيل إن القائل موسى عليه السلام .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p435/r9.claim: An alternate reading has واتبع in place of وابتغ.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says this means seeking lawful earnings from what God has given.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r1.anchor: أحدهما : طلب الحلال في كسبه , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says this means giving charity and maintaining kinship ties.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه الصدقة وصلة الرحم , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r3.claim: Mawardi offers a broader possibility: use God's blessings to draw near to Him; the hereafter means Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r3.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : وهو أعم أن يتقرب بنعم الله إليه , والمراد بالدار الآخرة الجنة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says not to forget one's share of worldly life means working in it for the hereafter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r4.anchor: أحدها : لا تنس حظك من الدنيا أن تعمل فيها لآخرتك , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r5.claim: Qatada says to be satisfied with what God made lawful and avoid what He prohibited.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r5.anchor: الثاني : لا تنس استغناك بما أحل الله لك عما حرمه عليك , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd explains this as remembering God's blessings and thanking Him through obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r6.anchor: الثالث : لا تنس ما أنعم الله عليك أن تشكره عليه بالطاعة وهذا معنى قول ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r7.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r7.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says to do good by fulfilling what God has made obligatory, as God has bestowed His favor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r7.anchor: الثاني : وأحسن فيما افترض الله عليك كما أحسن في إنعامه عليك , وهذا معنى قول يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r8.claim: Another gloss is to seek lawful provision as God has made lawful provision available to you.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r8.anchor: الثالث : أحسن في طلب الحلال كما أحسن إليك في الإحلال .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r9.claim: One possible meaning is not to commit acts of disobedience on earth.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r10.claim: A second, unexplained gloss is simply do not cut off.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says God does not love the deeds of corrupters.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r11.anchor: أحدهما : لا يحب أعمال المفسدين , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r12.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r12.claim: Ibn Qutayba says God does not draw near to corrupters.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p267/r12.anchor: الثاني : لا يقرب المفسدين , قاله ابن قتيبة .

MUJAHID:v2p490/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p490/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p490/r1.claim: One's share of this world is the opportunity to act there in obedience to God.
MUJAHID:v2p490/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا ﴾ يقول لا تنس العمل فيها بطاعتي

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r5.claim: Qarun should use the wealth and good God gave him to seek the hereafter, meaning the Garden.

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r6.claim: Do not forget your portion means do not abandon your share of worldly life: working in it for the hereafter.
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r6.anchor: { ولا تنس نصيبك } يعني ولا تترك حظك { من الدنيا } أن تعمل فيها لآخرتك

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r7.claim: Doing good means giving charity and doing good works in ways that please God.
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r7.anchor: { وأحسن } العطية في الصدقة والخير فيما يرضى الله عز وجل

MUQATIL:28:76-78/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:76-78/r8.claim: Do not commit disobedience in response to God’s beneficence; God does not love corrupters.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r1.claim: Use the wealth and abundance God gave you to seek the Hereafter through charity to the poor, maintaining kinship, and other good works.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r1.anchor: بأن تتصدق على الفقراء وتصل الرحم ونصرف إلى أبواب الخير

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r2.claim: One view is to take from this world what suffices and benefits you.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r2.anchor: وهو أن تأخذ ما يكفيك ويصلحك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r3.claim: Another view is to use worldly means to attain the Hereafter, which is the believer's share of this world.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه وأطاب بدنياك آخرتك فإن ذلك حظ المؤمن منها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r4.claim: Do good to God's servants; alternatively, show gratitude and obedience to the Creator for His beneficence.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r4.anchor: أو أحسن بشكرك وطاعتك لخالق الأنام كما أحسن إليك بالإنعام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p246/r5.claim: Seeking corruption in the land means acting unjustly and transgressing.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r22.claim: Use the worldly gifts God gave to seek Paradise, directing worldly means to the afterlife rather than tyranny.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r22.anchor: أي اطلب فيما أعطاك الله من الدنيا الدار الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r23.speaker: ابن عباس والجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r23.claim: Ibn Abbas and most commentators say not to waste one’s lifetime without righteous works, since life and good deeds are one’s worldly share.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r23.anchor: قال ابن عباس والجمهور: لا تضيع عمرك في ألا تعمل عملا صالحا

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r24.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r24.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say not to neglect lawful enjoyment, seeking it, or prudently considering worldly welfare.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r24.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: معناه لا تضيع حظك من دنياك في تمتعك بالحلال

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r25.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r25.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the softer reading allows the desired worldly good and avoids admonition so harsh that it alienates the addressee.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r26.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r26.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r26.claim: Ibn ʿUmar combines worldly and afterlife effort: cultivate worldly life as if living forever, and work for the afterlife as if dying tomorrow.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r26.anchor: قلت: وهذان التأويلان قد جمعهما ابن عمر في قوله: احرث لدنياك كأنك تعيش أبدا

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r27.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r27.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r27.claim: Al-Hasan advises giving away surplus while keeping what suffices.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r27.anchor: وعن الحسن: قدم الفضل، وأمسك ما يبلغ

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r28.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r28.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r28.claim: Malik says one’s worldly share is eating and drinking without extravagance.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r28.anchor: وقال مالك: هو الأكل والشرب بلا سرف

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r29.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r29.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#4/r29.claim: Another view says the worldly share to remember is the shroud, since it is what remains of one’s possessions.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r1.claim: The first cited poem says that all one gathers leaves only two shrouds and embalming materials.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r2.claim: A second poem says the owner of all the world departs with nothing but cotton and a shroud.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r3.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi calls Qatada’s reading best: one’s share of worldly life is its lawful portion.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r3.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وأبدع ما فيه عندي قول قتادة: ولا تنس نصيبك الحلال

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r4.claim: Doing good as God did good means obeying and worshipping Him in response to His favor.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r4.anchor: أي أطع الله واعبده كما أنعم عليك

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r5.claim: The Prophetic definition of ihsan is to worship God as though one sees Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r5.anchor: ومنه الحديث: ما الإحسان؟ قال: " أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه "

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r6.claim: Another explanation makes the command an instruction to give alms to the poor.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r7.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi says the many interpretations converge on using God’s blessings in obedience to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r7.anchor: قال ابن العربي: فيه أقوال كثيرة جماعها استعمال نعم الله في طاعة الله

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r8.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r8.claim: Malik says the command permits eating and drinking without extravagance.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r8.anchor: وقال مالك: الأكل والشرب من غير سرف

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r9.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi reads Malik as answering excessive asceticism: the Prophet enjoyed sweets, honey, roast meat, and cold water.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r9.anchor: قال ابن العربي: أرى مالكا أراد الرد على الغالين في العبادة والتقشف

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r10.claim: Seeking corruption in the land means committing sins.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:76-77#5/r11.claim: God does not love those who commit corruption.
